problem.text: SafetensorsCollection previously resolved tensor reads only through its file index. This change adds an in-memory source without replacing the existing disk loader.

reasoning.text: The new source is a mutable overlay: set_new_tensors stores the supplied object directly, and matching memory keys take precedence over file keys. Missing memory keys still use the existing file path.

impact.text: Single-tensor presence checks and reads accept memory tensors, but sizing, listing, prefix reads and close explicitly assert that new_tensors is None. Even an empty dictionary activates these restrictions; passing None restores the file-only interface.

source_notes.text: The earlier inventory entry describes list_tensors as a header-derived metadata interface. The new assertions make that interface unavailable while a memory mapping is installed.

Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports an extension import failure and the reporter's environment workaround, not a request for memory loading. No connection to this change is established.

limitations: No PyTorch tensor transfers, model loading, native I/O or GPU execution were tested. The Python check transcribed only dictionary membership logic.
The change supplies no usage example or mapping validation. End-to-end lifecycle compatibility with the restricted metadata and close methods remains untested.
The native failure-path observation is source-derived, not a reproduced deadlock.

chapters.title: Memory-first tensor lookup with a restricted collection interface

claims.text: Construction still scans the directory and builds file metadata before initializing new_tensors to None. set_new_tensors assigns a mapping rather than merging it into tensor_file_map, so file metadata remains separate.

get_tensor first resolves an omitted device to CPU, then returns new_tensors[key].to(device) for a memory hit. This bypasses file opening, payload validation, loading metrics and the file branch's BF16-to-FP16 conversion. Consequently allow_bf16 does not control the memory branch's dtype.

Memory misses retain required-versus-optional file lookup behavior: absent required keys raise ValueError, while optional keys return None. Existing mt_fread and python implementations remain the fallback alternatives.

has_tensor_group evaluates an entire group separately against each source, rather than against their union. String subkeys are required members; nested alternatives need at least one match. Linear.is_exl3_storage uses this predicate for sv/svh, su/suh and trellis before load_exl3 fetches individual tensors.

A bounded transcription returned false for a group with trellis only on disk and su/sv only in memory, although every individual key was available. Putting the complete group in either source returned true.

This design offers inexpensive memory overrides but not a fully interchangeable memory-backed collection: group completeness is source-local and metadata operations are deliberately guarded rather than synthesized from tensors.

The earlier loading entry records a native read-failure synchronization risk. Inspection of the parent implementation and this single-file diff shows that the risky wait/error logic is carried over unchanged for disk fallback; memory hits bypass it.

findings.description: Group detection does not compose the same disk-plus-memory availability offered by individual lookup.
findings.trigger: A requested group is complete only across the union of tensor_file_map and new_tensors, for example disk trellis plus memory su and sv.
findings.expected_behavior: If group detection is intended to reflect individual lookup availability, this group would be recognized.
findings.actual_behavior: has_tensor_group returns false because neither source independently contains the complete group. Linear.load_exl3 consequently declines that storage layout.

verification.description: Whole-parent literal search found direct application callers in Linear.load_fp16 and Linear.is_exl3_storage; load_exl3 checks the latter before reading tensors. The multi-member EXL3 group is the concrete affected case.
verification.limits: Whether source-local completeness is intentional is unestablished; no model workflow was executed.

verification.description: Transcribed the changed predicate and checked split-source and complete-source groups.
verification.limits: Standard-library membership test only, not repository or tensor execution.

findings.description: The existing native disk fallback can leave its GPU copy worker waiting after a read failure.
findings.trigger: A GPU-target mt_fread load has a copy worker waiting on an empty queue when a reader fails, with no subsequent successful enqueue.
findings.expected_behavior: The failure should wake the copy worker and allow the loader to report its I/O error.
findings.actual_behavior: The reader only sets load_failed; the wait predicate checks only queue nonemptiness and receives no failure notification, so thread joining may not complete.

verification.description: Whole-parent search located the binding and get_tensor's native call. The task leaves this fallback unchanged while bypassing it on memory hits.
verification.limits: No concurrent execution or injected I/O failure; CPU and python-loader paths do not use this copy-worker wait.

annotation.summary: Adds memory-first tensor lookup with disk fallback, while restricting collection metadata operations and requiring tensor groups to be complete within one source.
